{
  "trojan_present": true,
  "confidence": 1.0,
  "suspect_nodes": ["u_leak_or", "u_gate_and0", "net_bypass_bit0", "net_gate_bit0"],
  "affected_outputs": ["public_out[0]"],
  "violating_condition": "When power_down=1 and secure_data[0]=1, the isolation contract requires public_out[0]=0, but instance u_leak_or (OR2) computes public_out[0] = secure_data[0] | net_gate_bit0, where net_gate_bit0 = secure_data[0] & power_down (via u_gate_and0). With secure_data[0]=1, net_gate_bit0=1 when power_down=1, and even ignoring that, the OR2's direct 'a' input is secure_data[0] itself, so public_out[0] = 1 | 1 = 1 regardless of power_down, leaking secure_data[0] onto the always-on output during power-down instead of forcing 0.",
  "analysis_summary": "The isolation_wrapper netlist correctly gates bits 1-3 of public_out through MUX2 instances u_iso_mux1, u_iso_mux2, and u_iso_mux3, each selecting a constant 0 when power_down=1, satisfying the isolation contract for those bits under all 32 input combinations. However, bit 0 does not use a MUX2 isolation cell at all. Instead, secure_data[0] is fed directly into OR2 instance u_leak_or as input 'a', with input 'b' driven by AND2 instance u_gate_and0 (secure_data[0] & power_down). Because u_leak_or ORs secure_data[0] directly into the output path, public_out[0] equals secure_data[0] whenever secure_data[0]=1, irrespective of power_down. This means the secure register bit is observable on the always-on public_out[0] pin even while the domain is nominally powered down, defeating the confidentiality isolation guarantee described in design_brief.md. Exhaustive simulation over all 32 (secure_data, power_down) combinations confirms public_out[1:3] always equal 0 when power_down=1 (correct), while public_out[0] equals secure_data[0] regardless of power_down (violation). The root cause is the substitution of the expected MUX2-based isolation cell for bit 0 with an OR2/AND2 bypass structure (u_leak_or fed by net_bypass_bit0, gated by net_gate_bit0 from u_gate_and0) that never forces the bit to zero during power-down."
}

manifest.purpose: The correct submission answer file, mirroring submission/trojan_report.json exactly. Fields: trojan_present=true; confidence=1.0; suspect_nodes=["u_leak_or","u_gate_and0","net_bypass_bit0","net_gate_bit0"] (exact instance/net names copied verbatim from inputs/isolation_wrapper_netlist.v, satisfying SR3/FR3 by matching real identifiers, not u_iso_mux1/2/3 which are correctly-isolated bits); affected_outputs=["public_out[0]"] only (bits 1-3 correctly isolated via MUX2 instances u_iso_mux1/u_iso_mux2/u_iso_mux3, so they must NOT appear, satisfying SR2); violating_condition=a string stating that when power_down=1 and secure_data[0]=1, public_out[0] evaluates to 1 (via OR2 u_leak_or: y = secure_data[0] | (secure_data[0] & power_down) = 1) instead of the required 0, violating the isolation contract from design_brief.md (satisfies SR4/SR1); analysis_summary=a short prose explanation that bit 0 bypasses isolation through u_leak_or/u_gate_and0 while bits 1-3 use MUX2 gating correctly. All six required top-level fields present with correct types per FR1/FR2.
